titlePlain: A Multi-Cloud Strategy That Cost More Than It
subtitle: Lesson 31 · Case Study · Illustrative scenario, not a real company

steps.label: "Never be locked into one cloud"
steps.sub: Adopted as architectural law, applied to every workload

steps.label: No cost model up front
steps.sub: A principle, not a tradeoff evaluated the way Lesson 8 recommends

steps.label: Every new system: Azure and AWS
steps.sub: Regardless of what the workload actually needed

code:
Duplicated tooling  -> two of every dashboard, policy engine, pipeline
Duplicated skills   -> every role effectively became two roles
Unmodeled egress    -> full replicas kept current across clouds
No real requirement -> most workloads never needed any of this
caption: None of these was one bad decision -- each was individually defensible, and they compounded.

eyebrow: What the savings were supposed to be

steps.label: Claimed benefit
steps.sub: Pricing leverage, protection against a single-provider outage

steps.label: What actually happened
steps.sub: No real leverage gained; no outage the architecture meaningfully protected against

steps.label: What recurred every month
steps.sub: Duplicated tooling, staffing, and egress costs -- regardless

code:
Blanket policy:      every workload -> multi-cloud, no cost model
Workload-by-workload: most workloads -> one cloud, by default
                      few workloads with a real, costed case
                      -> deliberate multi-cloud duplication
caption: Multi-cloud wasn't the mistake -- treating it as one-size-fits-all was.
